title: cedar-bay-payments-integration-call-notes-2026-03-31
content:
Cedar Bay Payments - Integration kickoff (working notes)
Date: 2026-03-30
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Cedar Bay - Head of Integrations), Priya Shah (Cedar Bay - SecOps), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE - owner), Priya Kapoor (Redwood Solutions), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood Infra), Elena Rodriguez (Redwood PM)

Summary / high-level:
- Customer is a mid-market payments processor (Cedar Bay) evaluating Redwood for transaction enrichment, fraud scoring, and conversational support for merchant ops.
- Primary constraints: PCI-ish data handling, strict latency reqs for enrichment call in payment flow, and desire for private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with strict data residency.
- Wants fast PoC (4–6 weeks) with representative traffic and an SLA conversation after PoC.

Key requirements called out by customer:
- Latency: enrichment endpoint must be <= 200ms p95 (on path for authorization flow) — they stated 150ms target in some flows but agreed 200ms p95 as initial SLO for discussion.
- Security & compliance: no raw PAN or full card numbers to be stored by Redwood; prefer tokenized payloads stored for embeddings. KMS integration + audit logs required.
- Networking: VPC peering or private link required; will not allow public internet egress for tokens.
- Data residency: primary infra in us-east-1; backup region eu-west-1 for DR.
- Throughput: peak 220 requests/sec for enrichment endpoint; average 60 req/sec. Typical request size ~ 200 tokens (input) and 100 tokens generated (small).
- Auth: prefer mTLS for service-to-service; also will use OIDC for admin/UI access.
- Model expectations: they want to start with a smaller curated model (cost conscious) for enrichment and evaluate higher-capacity model for fraud/reranking. Embeddings for merchant similarity (vector DB in their infra).

Technical notes / gotchas:
- Latency vs throughput tradeoff: to hit 200ms p95 at 220 rps we will almost certainly need Dedicated capacity with pinned GPUs and aggressive batching disabled for the critical path. Marcus: estimate sizing below.
- KV cache usefulness: Most enrichment requests have repeat prefixes (merchant metadata). Suggest prefix/KV cache to reduce compute for repeated tokens. But KV cache requires sticky routing on Dedicated; add note for routing policy.
- Tokenization & PCI: we must ensure customer strips or tokenizes PAN before sending. Redwood must not store raw PANs; embeddings to be generated only from hashed/tokenized fields. Add explicit contract phrasing.
- Private network: VPC peering + private endpoints required. Marcus to confirm whether Private deployment (customer-managed) or Redwood Dedicated with private link is quicker. Customer prefers Redwood-managed but private network.
- KMS/HSM: Priya Shah asked about bringing their KMS key (BYOK). Redwood supports KMS integrations; need to confirm BYOK flow and key wrap for embeddings at rest.
- Audit logs: they require 12 months retention for event logs related to admin actions and data access. This is an enterprise add-on.
- Fallback: They want deterministic fallback if high latency — e.g., fallback to cached response or a smaller model. Need to document rollback/fallback policies in the SLA.

Sizing / initial capacity (back-of-envelope) — Marcus / infra:
- Target latency: 200ms p95 at 220 rps, avg request 200 tokens in, 100 out.
- Option A (Dedicated, larger model): 4x A100-equivalent workers, autoscale cushion 30% (peak headroom).
- Option B (Private small quantized model): 6x smaller GPUs with quantized 8-bit runtime to reduce cost — fewer tokens/sec per GPU but cheaper.
- Marcus: follow-up to run perf sim with realish payloads (customer to share sample traces). Estimated time to confirm: 5 business days after sample traffic received.

API / Integration details:
- Suggested endpoints: /v1/enrich (sync, low-latency), /v1/score (async/batched for fraud scoring), /v1/embeddings (streamed, customer-managed vector DB).
- Auth: mTLS cert exchange for service calls; OIDC for UI. Provide cert rotation doc.
- Rate limits: we will throttle background scoring; enrichment is prioritized route with guaranteed throughput on Dedicated.
- Observability: will expose per-route latency, token-cost, and tracing headers (x-request-id) for correlation. Need sampling decisions to avoid PII in logs.

Privacy & data handling decisions needed:
- Customer must strip PANs / PII before sending. If they need Redwood to handle PAN -> requires full PCI contract and different product tier.
- Embeddings: hashes only; no reversible PII should be kept in vector DB.
- Retention: default 30 days for traces/payloads; can extend to 12 months for logs only (enterprise add-on).

Open questions (to resolve in next week):
- Customer to confirm whether they will tokenize before sending or expect Redwood to tokenization service. (Alex to confirm by 2026-04-05)
- BYOK: can Cedar Bay provide KMS key and what is Redwood's expected on-boarding flow? (Security owners to define; Priya Kapoor + Priya Shah sync)
- Sample traffic: customer to share 3 days of sampled traffic (anonymized) so Marcus can run perf sims. (Alex to share by 2026-04-02)
- SLA numbers: finalize p95 SLO and error budget; will likely be higher-cost tier — draft SLA to be proposed after PoC.

Next steps / action items (owners + ETA):
- Jordan: write short PoC plan + tech design (network, auth, model selection, data flow) and send to Cedar Bay and internal team. ETA: 2026-04-03.
- Marcus: perf sims once sample traffic available; provide recommended Dedicated sizing and cost estimate. ETA: 5 business days after samples.
- Priya Kapoor: draft initial SLA + compliance checklist (KMS, audit retention, data residency) for review. ETA: 2026-04-10.
- Alex (Cedar Bay): share anonymized sample traffic + confirm tokenization approach. ETA: 2026-04-02.
- Elena: create Confluence page and tracker for integration tasks (link: CONFLUENCE-CCP-cedar-bay-integration).

Risks / blockers:
- If customer cannot tokenize PANs, we'll need a separate PCI onboarding that pushes timeline out 8–12 weeks.
- Private connectivity approvals from their network team may take time; suggest pre-start with hosted test harness using synthetic data to parallelize work.

Notes for follow-up call:
- Walk through PoC plan, discuss minimal scope for enrichment (strict latency path) vs secondary scoring path, confirm sample traffic format (JSON schema), and agree on security questionnaire answers.
- Confirm which Redwood contacts will be the technical points of contact for network + security (Marcus + Priya Kapoor).

Misc small items / scratchpad thoughts:
- Consider recommending prefix-caching for merchant metadata; reduces per-token compute ~30% on repeat flows.
- Evaluate small distilled model (redwood-distil-1) for enrichment initial PoC — cheaper and likely meets quality for enrichment transforms.
- If customer uses per-merchant templates -> use structured outputs + function-calling to keep responses deterministic.

End of notes.

-- Jordan
